unit_statements_verbatim: The minor requires at least 20 units.

notes.text: The Minor in Geodesign expands students’ perspectives as they prepare for careers in architecture, communications, environmental studies, health promotion, public policy, real estate, social sciences, and urban planning. Emphasizing the value of interdisciplinary collaboration within urban spaces, the program is grounded in the spatial sciences and includes one lower-division elective, four core courses, and a capstone course. Together, these interconnected courses train future leaders in sustainability to apply spatial principles that foster connected and resilient communities. Students gain both conceptual and practical skills, ranging from spatial data analysis to stakeholder engagement, that help them understand local and global phenomena. The program equips students to address pressing environmental and social challenges with data-driven solutions and cultivates an appreciation for how urban structures develop across space and time.
